newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen weaker after overnight fall.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen weaker after overnight fall.

text.p: FUTURE RANGE/DAY SPPRT RSTNC RSI-9 MA-5 MA-25
OUTLOOK OF BOJ OPERATION AT 0020 GMT: drainage of 100 bln yen

*Japanese government bond futures expected to open lower following overnight weakness triggered by key Finance Ministry official's remarks. *Key June contract fell as low as 126.47 on LIFFE after closing at 126.76 in Tokyo on Wednesday.
Sakakibara said he could not understand why Japan's long-term interest rates were at their current record-low levels.
"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," he said.
Traders said June futures were likely to open lower but the downside may hold around 126.20 or 126.30.
"Investor bargain-hunting interest is likely to emerge if June dips below 126.50," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The BOJ is widely expected to continue its accommodative stance in Thursday's regular money market operation, but the impact on JGBs is likely to be limited, traders said.

The central bank unexpectedly refrained from its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation on Wednesday, leaving the market in surplus by about 200 billion yen. However, this move had limited impact on JGBs.
"The BOJ is likely to maintain an accommodative stance today, but such a move is unlikely to move the JGB market," said a trader at another city bank's securities unit.
